A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HyperGraphRAG and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–I. The material supports a reliable comparison throughout.

before.justification: v2 reports original five-domain evaluations, component ablations, retrieval analyses, generation-quality scores, time/cost measurements, and a medical case study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix H, including Tables 2, 3, and 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A/C retain the same extraction, bipartite storage, vector retrieval, neighborhood expansion, and chunk-fused generation procedures. The revised chunk count is an experimental setting change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Medicine, Agriculture, CS, Legal, and Mix, retaining Binary Source and N-ary Source questions constructed through one-to-three-hop sampling. No evaluated domain or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same comparisons retain NaiveGeneration, StandardRAG, GraphRAG, LightRAG, PathRAG, and HippoRAG2. The construction analysis also retains its GraphRAG and LightRAG comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes chunk retrieval k_C from 6 to 5. Appendix G and Table 4 likewise change StandardRAG from six to five chunks, covering the main and time/cost evaluations. This establishes a reported setting revision, but does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The component ablations, knowledge-structure analysis, retrieval-count and context-length sensitivity experiments, generation analysis, and Appendix H medical case study are retained without additional or revised analyses.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting remains unchanged. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 and Figures 4–7 retain their numerical results and qualitative findings. For example, HyperGraphRAG's reported Medicine overall F1 remains 35.35. These unchanged reports do not establish a performance effect from the revised chunk setting.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Propositions 1–3, Appendix B proofs, Appendix C complexity analyses, and evaluation formulas are retained. Differences in mathematical spacing do not revise their reasoning.

C1.justification: The method contribution and cross-domain performance claims remain unchanged. Although the abstract changes 'a novel' to 'the first' hypergraph-based RAG method, the equivalent priority claim already appears in Section 2 of v2.

C2.justification: The introduction replaces 'representation loss and sparsity' with 'representation sparsity' when interpreting binary decomposition of the medical example. This is a limited local narrowing; the broader information-loss argument, experimental interpretations, and Appendix I limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The documented chunk-count hyperparameter changes consistently from six to five in Section 5.1, Appendix G, and Table 4. Prompts, pseudocode, model and hardware details, and other settings remain unchanged. The same code/data URL moves into a footnote without changing access information.

R1.justification: The same 29 cited works and related-work positioning are retained. Reference 28 abbreviates its author list, and the abstract repeats a priority claim already present in v2; neither introduces a new relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 makes short abstract/introduction edits, corrects 'Generation Equality' to 'Generation Quality' in the Section 5.6 heading, adds acknowledgments, and updates affiliation, contact, and conference information. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures and table structures are retained. Moving the repository URL into a footnote and inserting acknowledgments cause limited reflow, including moving reference 14 onto page 11. Text and equation spacing also change slightly.

improvement.justification: Editorial corrections and funding disclosure provide small benefits, while the scientific evidence and proofs remain unchanged. However, the six-to-five chunk revision accompanies identical results in Tables 2 and 3 without identifying a documentation correction or rerun. Whether this improves reproducibility or associates existing results with an altered protocol is unresolved, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
